title: Social Media Star Niharika NM Makes Bollywood Debut in Bhai Tera Star Hai
excerpt: The content creator-turned-actress, who walked away from a thriving social media career with over 6 million followers, stars alongside Raghav Juyal in the London-set comedy releasing July 31.
body:
• Niharika NM, known for her South Indian mom comedy sketches, makes her Hindi film debut in Bhai Tera Star Hai alongside Raghav Juyal, releasing July 31.
  • The Chapman University graduate stopped creating content three years ago to train as an actress, signing seven films in her first year across Tamil, Telugu, and Hindi cinema.
  • She holds a three-film deal with Karthik Subbaraj's Stone Bench Creations and already debuted in Telugu (Mithra Mandali) and Tamil (Perusu).
  • Niharika was the first Indian creator to guest on Netflix's animated series Big Mouth, alongside Jordan Peele and Megan Thee Stallion.

Niharika NM built her name making millions laugh with comedy sketches about South Indian moms. Now she's betting her career on a different kind of screen. The social media creator, who amassed over 6 million followers across platforms, stars opposite Raghav Juyal in Bhai Tera Star Hai, a London-set comedy-drama hitting theatres on July 31. It marks her entry into Bollywood after already debuting in Telugu and Tamil cinema over the past year.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Zy8KDEJU3iY

From Viral Reels to the Big Screen

The transition was deliberate — and costly. Three years ago, at the peak of her social media career, Niharika stopped making content entirely to focus on acting.

"I stopped making content probably three years ago, and it was a risk I was willing to take at the peak of my social media career. I know how to build myself back up. That much faith I have in myself."

— Niharika NM, actress and content creator

Born in Chennai, raised in Bengaluru, with parents rooted in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, Niharika grew up across languages and cultures. She pursued an MBA and MFA at Chapman University in California, where her theater background deepened. After locking in a corporate job in the US, she returned to India for a few shoots — and never went back.

"I wanted to fully jump into acting because I wanted to really learn," she told Zoom TV Entertainment. Her training included a year and a half under Shanoo Sharma, the casting director associated with Yash Raj Films, before she started auditioning.

Seven Films in Year One

The auditions converted fast. Niharika signed a three-film deal with director Karthik Subbaraj's Stone Bench Creations, the production house behind Jigarthanda DoubleX and the Suriya-starrer Retro. Additional projects followed with Geetha Arts, S Originals and Waltair Productions, and Lyca Productions — seven films locked in her first year as an actress, according to The Hollywood Reporter India.

Her Telugu debut came with Mithra Mandali in October 2025, followed by the Tamil dark comedy Perusu, produced by Stone Bench Films alongside Baweja Studios. She also learned Malayalam for an upcoming role, adding to the Telugu, Tamil, and Kannada she grew up speaking. Hindi, she has said, is the language she picked up most recently.

Bhai Tera Star Hai: The Bollywood Entry

Directed by Vivek B. Agrawal, Bhai Tera Star Hai follows Ajay Singh (Raghav Juyal), a delusional aspiring actor in London who loses money in a betting scheme and gets entangled with gangsters. Niharika plays Rashmi, a character she describes as "feisty, flippant but all heart." The ensemble cast includes Sanjay Kapoor, Barkha Singh, Chandan Roy Sanyal, Vivan Bhatena, and Vikalp Mehta.

The film is targeting 900 to 1,000 screens through distributor PVR INOX Pictures, according to Sacnilk — a significant count for a high-concept comedy opening against Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Both the director and Juyal pushed for a theatrical-only release, banking on audience appetite for fresh comedy after a stretch of heavy OTT content.

"It feels like seeing someone from your neighborhood make it. I'm so proud of him."

— Niharika NM, on sharing the screen with Raghav Juyal

A Crossover Career

Before cinema, Niharika had already crossed into American entertainment. She became the first Indian content creator to guest on Netflix's animated series Big Mouth, recording alongside Jordan Peele and Megan Thee Stallion. Her social media collaborations spanned Priyanka Chopra, Aamir Khan, and John Legend.

That crossover resume — Chapman University education, a Netflix credit, collaborations bridging Bollywood and Hollywood — makes her trajectory distinct from the typical influencer-to-actor pipeline. She trained formally, waited, and chose her projects across three film industries rather than chasing the quickest Bollywood break.

What It Means for the Diaspora

Niharika's path mirrors a journey familiar to many in the Indian diaspora: an American university degree, a corporate job lined up, and then the pull of creative ambition back home. Her decision to turn down a US career to pursue acting in India — starting in South Indian cinema before moving to Hindi films — offers a different model than the usual NRI-to-Bollywood narrative. Her multilingual range across Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Hindi, and now Malayalam reflects the cultural versatility many diaspora Indians recognize in their own families.

Looking Ahead

With Bhai Tera Star Hai opening this week and multiple South Indian projects in various stages of production, Niharika's schedule shows no sign of slowing. She has spoken about wanting to take on darker roles in Tamil cinema and dreams of working with S.S. Rajamouli and Mani Ratnam. For now, the question is whether her social media following — and her growing film credits — can translate into box office pull in a crowded release window.
nri_angle: Niharika NM's trajectory from a Chapman University MBA in California to a multilingual film career in India mirrors the creative pull many diaspora Indians feel toward opportunities back home.
